answer: Every new identity must post a bond of B POA that stays locked for a 48h cooldown before it can be re-minted. A sybil burst of N clones therefore ties up N x B capital frozen for two days: at the nadir of network growth, spinning 1000 sybils locks 1000 bonds and drags the attacker float down, while a single knoll of established agents can cross-match behavioral fingerprints and slash any duplicate that fails reveal. A sonnet of evasion scripts cannot retire a slashed bond early, so every fake identity carries an explicit sunk cost that scales linearly with the attack size.
